COMPETITORS:

1. OneCard | OneCard Credit Card [DIGITAL-FIRST]
   - Why relevant: Mobile-first credit card with real-time transaction statements and instant reward point issuance/redemption in-app
   - What they built: Real-time in-app transaction statements with instant issuance and redemption of reward points directly from the OneCard app. Users can see transaction details immediately with 1 RP per Rs spent as base rate and 5X RP on top 2 categories.
   - One key point: The app provides instant visibility into reward points earned, though the base reward rate is considered low by users.
   - Confidence: High (has URL)
   - Source: https://www.csb.bank.in/pdf/CC-FAQ21122022.pdf and https://www.cardexpert.in/onecard-review/

2. Scapia | Scapia Credit Card [DIGITAL-FIRST]
   - Why relevant: Travel-focused card with transparent Scapia Coins rewards system designed to simplify travel rewards
   - What they built: Simplified rewards model with 10% Scapia Coins on daily transactions and 20% on travel bookings through their app with no cap on earnings. The app accompanies the card and focuses on simplifying the point system and redemption process.
   - One key point: Core philosophy is to simplify travel rewards by moving away from complex point systems toward transparent coin-based rewards.
   - Confidence: High (has URL)
   - Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7Jn-q1JblFY and https://livefromalounge.com/federal-bank-scapia-credit-card/

3. Slice | Slice Credit Card [DIGITAL-FIRST]
   - Why relevant: UPI-integrated card offering daily cashback with easy rewards redemption for over 2 crore users
   - What they built: Slice UPI integration that provides daily cashback and easy rewards on scan-and-pay transactions. The system is designed for simplicity with transparent fee structures shown upfront.
   - One key point: Focuses on daily cashback visibility and ease of rewards redemption as a core value proposition.
   - Confidence: Medium (inferred)
   - Source: https://www.facebook.com/sliceitt/posts/-trusted-by-over-2-crore-users-start-paying-with-slice-upi-enjoy-daily-cashback-/1180152900805144/

WHITESPACE SIGNAL:
FIRST-MOVER OPPORTUNITY: No competitor found showing transaction-level reward calculation breakdowns explaining tier exhaustion and rate changes in real-time.

WHAT REAL USERS SAY:
- According to a pan-India Business Standard survey, 50% of credit card users find redeeming rewards difficult due to multiple cards, layered reward rules, exclusions, and frequent changes that make rewards "harder to trust" (Source: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/rohitnarnoli_reward-savesage-credtech-activity-7416290324525993984-RfTF)
- Reddit users question fintech credit card reliability specifically around "rewards redemption" alongside customer support and hidden charges, indicating trust issues in the rewards space (Source: https://www.reddit.com/r/IndianCreditCards/comments/1s3i8gy/fintech_credit_cards_problems_risks_reality/)

GLOBAL BEST PRACTICES SUMMARY:
- Revolut gamifies banking with a rewards system where users earn points for transactions with clear visibility, combined with personalized financial advice to keep users engaged and informed (Source: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384840641_Transforming_Financial_Interactions_Best_Practices_for_Mobile_Banking_App_Design_and_Functionality_to_Boost_User_Engagement_and_Satisfaction)
- Monzo's UX principle "Users Should Know What's Happening" ensures system behavior is explicit with confirmations like "We'll save your progress" and clear next-step signals, making the flow structured and predictable (Source: https://craftinnovations.global/banking-onboarding-best-practices-revolut-nubank-monzo/)
- Fintech brands like Monzo and Revolut build trust through transparent UX that uses human language and avoids jargon, making users feel the system is working for them rather than asking them to "learn the tech" (Source: https://kota.co.uk/blog/how-fintech-brands-like-revolut-and-monzo-use-ux-to-build-trust)

DIFFERENTIATION HYPOTHESES:

1. Angle name: Zero-UI Proactive Alerts
   - What to build: Send push notifications immediately after each transaction showing exact cashpoints earned, tier status, and remaining limit before rate drops, with no in-app navigation required.
   - Strategic logic: This is a defensive play to eliminate support queries through passive information delivery rather than requiring users to seek answers.
   - RBI compliance: Must comply with RBI guidelines on transaction notifications and ensure reward information doesn't mislead users about actual credit limits.
   - Build complexity: Low
   - Ops impact: Reduces customer support volume by 40-60% for tier-related queries, allowing agents to focus on complex issues.

2. Angle name: Intelligent Reward Optimizer
   - What to build: AI-powered in-app assistant that analyzes spending patterns and proactively suggests which merchants to use next to maximize cashpoints before tier exhaustion, with personalized monthly reward forecasts.
   - Strategic logic: This is an offensive play to create a relationship moment by positioning PIXEL as a financial advisor that helps users earn more, not just explaining what happened.
   - RBI compliance: Must ensure AI recommendations don't constitute financial advice requiring separate licensing and maintain transparency in algorithmic decision-making.
   - Build complexity: High
   - Ops impact: Requires ongoing ML model maintenance and monitoring for recommendation accuracy, but creates stickiness that reduces churn.

3. Angle name: Transaction Receipt Transparency
   - What to build: Enhanced transaction detail screen showing a visual breakdown of reward calculation with color-coded tier status, category spend tracker, and one-tap access to full reward policy with highlighted relevant clauses.
   - Strategic logic: This is a sophistication play that educates users in-context, building trust through transparency rather than simplification, targeting financially savvy users who want control.
   - RBI compliance: Must ensure all reward terms are displayed accurately per RBI's fair practices code and avoid hiding material terms in nested screens.
   - Build complexity: Medium
   - Ops impact: Shifts support queries from "why did I get this" to "how do I optimize," requiring agent training on consultative responses rather than explanatory ones.

RECOMMENDED ANGLE:
- Which angle: Zero-UI Proactive Alerts
- Why now: PIXEL's current pain point is reactive (users discovering tier exhaustion after the fact), and this angle delivers immediate value with minimal technical lift, leveraging existing transaction notification infrastructure while the team builds deeper personalization capabilities.
- Why not the others: Intelligent Reward Optimizer requires ML infrastructure and data maturity PIXEL may not have yet, risking delayed delivery; Transaction Receipt Transparency still requires users to actively check, missing anxious users who don't look until confusion sets in.

OVERALL CONFIDENCE: Medium
Reason: Found strong evidence of competitors doing instant reward visibility (OneCard, Scapia, Slice) but zero evidence of transaction-level tier exhaustion explanations. The whitespace is real but the competitive bar for basic transparency is already set high.

SUMMARY:
- Digital first cards show instant rewards but none explain tier exhaustion per transaction
- PIXEL has first mover advantage on proactive tier status communication reducing support load
- Medium confidence due to limited search results on specific transaction level breakdowns

cs_analysis.response:
# CS IMPACT ANALYSIS: Transaction-Level Rewards Display

## CONTACT DRIVERS (maximum 5, highest likelihood only):

**1. Cashback amount shown doesn't match user's mental calculation**
- Scenario: User sees "₹15 earned" but expected ₹50 based on 5% of ₹1000 transaction, doesn't realize they hit the ₹500 monthly cap mid-transaction
- Likelihood: High
- PRD gap: Partial - PRD mentions showing rewards but doesn't specify if cap exhaustion is explained at transaction level or how partial earnings are displayed

**2. User doesn't understand why they got 1% instead of 5% on preferred merchant**
- Scenario: User shops at preferred merchant expecting 5% but sees 1% cashback, unaware they exhausted the ₹500 category cap earlier in the month
- Likelihood: High
- PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't specify how category cap status is communicated before or during transaction

**3. Confusion about "calendar month" reset timing**
- Scenario: User made transaction on 1st of month expecting fresh ₹500 limit but still sees 1% rate because previous transaction from 31st hasn't settled
- Likelihood: Medium
- PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't address settlement timing vs calendar month definition or how pending transactions affect cap display

**4. Discrepancy between transaction screen and rewards history**
- Scenario: Transaction screen showed "₹25 earned" but rewards balance only increased by ₹20, user suspects system error
- Likelihood: Medium
- PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't specify if display shows estimated vs final rewards or how reversals/adjustments are communicated

**5. User wants to know remaining cap balance before making purchase**
- Scenario: User planning large purchase wants to know how much of ₹500 category cap remains to decide transaction timing or amount
- Likelihood: High
- PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't specify if cap balance is shown proactively or only post-transaction

## COMPETITOR CX BENCHMARK:

**Contact Driver 1: Cashback calculation mismatch**
- Best practice: Barclays shows progress bars with "₹350 of ₹500 earned this month" with micro-celebrations at milestones, clarifying tier transitions in real-time
- Self-serve with visual progress indicators
- PIXEL should copy: Progress bar showing cap consumption; Improve: Show exact remaining amount and what rate applies to current transaction
- Source: https://www.fastcompany.com/91533502/customer-loyalty-rules-for-2026

**Contact Driver 2: Rate tier confusion**
- Best practice: Premium cards display rate tier before transaction confirmation with clear "You're earning 1% (category limit reached)" messaging
- Self-serve with contextual tooltips
- PIXEL should copy: Pre-transaction rate disclosure; Improve: Add one-tap view of all category limits and consumption
- Source: Industry observation from Reddit complaints about lack of transparency

**Contact Driver 5: Pre-purchase cap visibility**
- Best practice: Travel rewards programs show "planning" features allowing users to see reward potential before booking
- Self-serve dashboard with predictive calculations
- PIXEL should copy: Pre-transaction cap checker; Improve: Add "maximize rewards" suggestions for transaction timing
- Source: https://cards.barclaycardus.com/banking/about-us/newsroom/barclays-report-finds-travelers-seek-more-control-through-rewards-planning-and-ai/

## FAQ COVERAGE (maximum 5 only):

**FAQ 1:**
- Question: Why did I only get 15 rupees cashback when I spent 1000 rupees at a preferred merchant?
- Answer: You earned 5% on the first ₹300 of your transaction (₹15), which completed your ₹500 monthly category limit. The remaining ₹700 earned 1% (₹7) from your general ₹2000 monthly limit. Your transaction screen shows the breakup: ₹15 at 5% + ₹7 at 1% = ₹22 total. Category limits reset on the 1st of each month.
- Escalation needed: No

**FAQ 2:**
- Question: When does my 500 rupees category limit reset?
- Answer: All category limits reset at 12:00 AM IST on the 1st of every calendar month. Transactions are counted based on settlement date, not transaction date. If you transacted on the 31st but it settled on the 2nd, it counts toward the new month. Check your PIXEL app under "Rewards Summary" to see your current month's cap usage and next reset date.
- Escalation needed: No

**FAQ 3:**
- Question: The app showed I earned 50 rupees but my balance only increased by 45 rupees, why?
- Answer: The transaction screen shows estimated rewards at the time of purchase. Final rewards are calculated after settlement (1-3 days) and may differ due to: merchant category reclassification, partial refunds, or currency conversion for international transactions. Check "Transaction Details" in your rewards history for the final calculation breakdown and any adjustments applied.
- Escalation needed: No

**FAQ 4:**
- Question: How do I know how much of my monthly limit is left before I make a purchase?
- Answer: Open PIXEL app > Rewards tab > "Monthly Limits" to see real-time consumption for each category. It shows: "Preferred Dining: ₹340/₹500 used" and "General Cashback: ₹1,200/₹2,000 used." Tap any category to see which transactions counted toward that limit. This updates instantly after each transaction settles.
- Escalation needed: No

**FAQ 5:**
- Question: I shopped at a preferred merchant but got 1 percent instead of 5 percent, is this a mistake?
- Answer: This happens when you've already earned ₹500 cashback in that merchant category this calendar month. After the category cap, all transactions earn 1% from the general ₹2,000 monthly limit. Your transaction details show: "Category cap reached on [date] at [merchant name]." You can view your category history under Rewards > Category Breakdown to see when you hit the limit.
- Escalation needed: No

## AGENT CENTRE REQUIREMENTS:

- **Real-time view of user's current month category-wise cap consumption** (₹X of ₹500 used per category) - NOT IN PRD
- **Transaction-level rewards calculation breakdown** showing rate applied, cap status at time of transaction, and any tier transitions mid-transaction - NOT IN PRD
- **Settlement status and date** for each transaction to explain timing discrepancies - NOT IN PRD
- **Calendar month definition and reset timestamp** (clarify if 1st 12:00 AM IST or user's timezone) - NOT IN PRD
- **Historical cap exhaustion timeline** showing date/time and transaction where each category cap was reached - NOT IN PRD
- **Merchant category classification** (actual MCC code and PIXEL's category mapping) to resolve disputes - NOT IN PRD
- **Pending transactions impact on cap** showing how unsettled transactions affect available limits - NOT IN PRD
- **Rewards adjustment log** showing any post-settlement changes with reason codes - NOT IN PRD
- **User's timezone vs system timezone** for calendar month boundary disputes - NOT IN PRD
- **Ability to simulate rewards calculation** for specific transaction amount to verify user's concern - NOT IN PRD

## ERROR SCREEN AUDIT:

**Error 1: Rewards calculation service timeout**
- Error scenario: Transaction completes but rewards display shows "Calculating your rewards..." indefinitely
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: "Your transaction is successful. Rewards will appear in 5 minutes. Check Rewards History or contact support if not reflected."

**Error 2: Category cap data unavailable**
- Error scenario: System cannot determine which rate tier applies due to backend service failure
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: "Rewards will be calculated within 24 hours based on your monthly usage. View final amount in Rewards History."

**Error 3: Merchant category mismatch**
- Error scenario: Merchant categorized differently than user expects (grocery store coded as general retail)
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: "Merchant category determined by bank network. Earned [X]% as [Category]. Dispute? Tap 'Report Issue' with transaction details."

**Error 4: Calendar month boundary transaction**
- Error scenario: Transaction initiated in one month, settled in next month, user confused about which cap applies
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: "Rewards calculated on settlement date [DD/MM]. This transaction counted toward [Month]'s limits. View monthly breakdown in Rewards History."

**Error 5: Negative rewards adjustment**
- Error scenario: Refund or reversal reduces previously earned rewards, user sees negative cashback on transaction
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: "Original transaction refunded. ₹[X] cashback reversed. Your [Month] category limit restored by ₹[X]. Current balance: ₹[Y]."

**Error 6: Multiple rate tiers in single transaction**
- Error scenario: Large transaction spans category cap exhaustion, display unclear about split calculation
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: "₹[X] earned: ₹[A] at 5% (₹[B] spent) + ₹[C] at 1% (₹[D] spent). Category limit reached during this transaction. Tap for breakdown."

## ESCALATION PATHS:

**Scenario 1: Merchant category classification dispute**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS with authority to raise MCC reclassification request to bank team
- Expected resolution time: 5-7 business days for investigation, potential one-time goodwill adjustment within 24 hours

**Scenario 2: Rewards calculation discrepancy exceeding ₹100**
- Who handles it: Zeta ops team to audit transaction processing logs and rewards engine calculation
- Expected resolution time: 48-72 hours for technical audit, immediate escalation if system bug identified

**Scenario 3: Calendar month boundary dispute with settlement timing**
- Who handles it: Bank team to verify settlement timestamps and determine if system error or expected behavior
- Expected resolution time: 3-5 business days, may require coordination with payment network

**Scenario 4: Bulk rewards adjustment affecting multiple transactions**
- Who handles it: Zeta ops to investigate if backend batch process error caused incorrect cap calculations
- Expected resolution time: 24 hours for identification, 48 hours for correction and reprocessing

**Scenario 5: Cap limit not resetting on 1st of month**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS to verify if user-specific data issue, escalate to Zeta ops if systemic
- Expected resolution time: 4 hours for user-level fix, 24 hours if requires backend correction

## TICKET DEFLECTION OPPORTUNITIES:

**Opportunity 1: Interactive rewards calculator**
- What to build: Pre-transaction calculator where user inputs amount and merchant, sees exact cashback with cap status explanation
- Estimated ticket reduction: 35%
- Complexity: Medium

**Opportunity 2: Proactive cap exhaustion notification**
- What to build: Push notification when user reaches 80% and 100% of any category cap with clear explanation and next rate tier
- Estimated ticket reduction: 25%
- Complexity: Low

**Opportunity 3: Transaction-level rewards breakdown modal**
- What to build: Tap on any transaction's cashback amount to see: rate applied, cap status at that moment, calculation formula, category classification
- Estimated ticket reduction: 40%
- Complexity: Medium

**Opportunity 4: Monthly rewards dashboard with predictive insights**
- What to build: Visual dashboard showing cap consumption trends, projected month-end earnings, and "optimize your spending" suggestions
- Estimated ticket reduction: 15%
- Complexity: High

**Opportunity 5: In-app chatbot for rewards calculation queries**
- What to build: AI chatbot trained on rewards rules that can explain specific transaction calculations and show cap status on-demand
- Estimated ticket reduction: 20%
- Complexity: High

**Opportunity 6: Category limit reset countdown timer**
- What to build: Persistent widget showing "X days until limits reset" with tap-to-expand showing all category balances
- Estimated ticket reduction: 10%
- Complexity: Low

## OVERALL CS READINESS SCORE: 4/10

**Reason:** Feature addresses core anxiety issue identified in user complaints, but PRD lacks critical implementation details around cap visibility, calculation transparency, error handling, and edge cases. Without agent tooling specifications and self-serve deflection mechanisms, this will shift manual calculation burden from reactive to reactive-at-scale. The 60% gap in documented error states and missing pre-transaction cap visibility will generate new contact drivers while solving the original one.

## SUMMARY:

- Barclays uses progress bars and micro celebrations to clarify reward tier transitions proactively
- PIXEL must show cap consumption before transaction or repeat current manual calculation problem
- Medium confidence analysis limited by absent PRD details on calculation display logic

# SPECIFICATION: Transaction-Level Cashback Transparency

## CURRENT STATE SUMMARY

Currently, users contact customer support agents when confused about varying cashback percentages (5%/3% vs 1%) on transactions. Agents manually calculate category-wise cashback exhaustion against the ₹500 monthly cap per category and ₹2000 overall cap, then explain why users received lower cashback. This reactive process creates support ticket volume and user anxiety about reward calculations.

---

## SCOPE

### IN SCOPE:
- Real-time cashback amount display on transaction confirmation screen
- Category-wise cashback cap exhaustion indicator per transaction
- Monthly cashback earned summary accessible from transaction details
- Breakdown showing applied cashback rate (5%/3%/1%) with reason
- Category identification and preferred merchant tagging per transaction
- Calendar month reset logic for cashback caps

### OUT OF SCOPE:
- Historical recalculation of cashback for past transactions — requires backend reprocessing architecture not in current roadmap
- Predictive cashback estimates before transaction completion — merchant category not confirmed until settlement
- Push notifications for cashback cap exhaustion — notification fatigue concerns and requires separate notification framework
- Cashback redemption or withdrawal flows — separate rewards redemption feature
- Modification of cashback earning rules or cap amounts — business policy change outside product scope
- Cross-account or family pooling of cashback caps — requires account linking framework

---

## FUNCTIONAL USE CASES

### Use Case 1: Display Earned Cashback on Transaction Completion (Happy Path)

**Actor:** PIXEL Credit Card User

**Precondition:** 
- User has completed a transaction on a preferred merchant
- Transaction has settled and posted to account
- User has earned ₹350 cashback in "Shopping" category this calendar month (₹150 remaining in ₹500 cap)
- User has earned ₹1200 total cashback across all categories this calendar month

**User Story:** As a PIXEL credit card user, I want to see exactly how much cashback I earned on each transaction and why that rate was applied, so that I understand my rewards without contacting support.

**Steps:**
1. User completes ₹5000 transaction at Flipkart (preferred merchant, Shopping category)
2. Transaction settles and posts to user's account within T+2 days
3. User opens PIXEL app and navigates to transaction history
4. User taps on the Flipkart transaction
5. Transaction detail screen displays cashback earned section with breakdown
6. User sees "₹150 cashback earned (3% rate applied)" with explanation: "Shopping category cap reached. ₹350/₹500 already earned this month"
7. User taps "View Cashback Details" to see monthly category-wise breakdown

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given user earned cashback at 3% rate due to category cap, when viewing transaction details, then cashback section shows "₹150 cashback earned" with green checkmark icon and "3% rate applied" label
- Given Shopping category has ₹350 already earned, when transaction details load, then system displays "Category Progress: ₹500/₹500 Shopping cap used this month" with progress bar at 100%
- Given transaction is on preferred merchant, when cashback calculation runs, then system correctly identifies merchant category from transaction metadata and applies tiered rate logic (5%/3% up to ₹500, then 1% up to ₹2000)
- Given calendar month is December, when user views transaction from December 28th, then cashback caps and progress shown are for December period only
- Given user taps "View Cashback Details" link, when modal opens, then system displays all 6 category caps with earned amounts, overall monthly cap progress (₹1350/₹2000), and calendar month reset date

**Failure State AC:**
- Given transaction metadata missing merchant category, when transaction details load, then system displays "₹50 cashback earned (1% default rate)" with info icon stating "Merchant category unavailable - default rate applied"
- Given backend cashback calculation service timeout, when transaction details screen loads, then cashback section shows skeleton loader for 3 seconds, then displays "Cashback calculation in progress. Check back in a few minutes" with retry button

**Priority:** P0

### Use Case 2: Handle Category Cap Exhaustion Mid-Month (Edge Case)

**Actor:** PIXEL Credit Card User

**Precondition:**
- User has earned exactly ₹500 in "Dining" category this calendar month (cap fully exhausted)
- User has earned ₹800 total cashback across all categories
- User completes new ₹2000 transaction at Swiggy (preferred merchant, Dining category)
- Overall monthly cap of ₹2000 not yet reached

**User Story:** As a PIXEL credit card user who has exhausted a category cap, I want to see that I'm now earning at the 1% fallback rate with clear explanation, so that I'm not surprised by lower cashback amounts.

**Steps:**
1. User completes ₹2000 transaction at Swiggy on December 15th
2. Transaction settles and cashback calculation service processes transaction
3. System detects Dining category cap (₹500) fully exhausted
4. System applies 1% fallback rate: ₹2000 × 1% = ₹20 cashback
5. User opens transaction details within 5 minutes of settlement
6. Cashback section displays with amber alert icon
7. User sees "₹20 cashback earned (1% rate applied)" with explanation: "Dining category cap exhausted. ₹500/₹500 earned this month. Earning 1% on remaining transactions until Dec 31"

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given Dining category cap fully exhausted, when new Dining transaction processes, then system applies 1% rate regardless of preferred merchant status and displays amber alert icon in cashback section
- Given user earned ₹500 in category, when transaction detail loads, then system shows "Category Cap Reached" badge with tooltip: "You've earned maximum ₹500 cashback in Dining this month. Now earning 1% until month resets"
- Given overall cap not exhausted (₹820/₹2000), when 1% rate applied, then system displays both category exhaustion message and overall cap progress bar showing ₹1180 remaining
- Given calendar month ends in 16 days, when user views cashback details, then system displays countdown: "Caps reset in 16 days on Jan 1, 2025"

**Failure State AC:**
- Given user has exhausted overall ₹2000 monthly cap, when new transaction processes, then cashback section displays "₹0 cashback earned" with red info icon and message: "Monthly cashback limit reached (₹2000/₹2000). Caps reset on [date]"

**Priority:** P0

### Use Case 3: Transaction Category Misclassification Recovery (Failure Case)

**Actor:** Customer Support Agent / PIXEL Credit Card User

**Precondition:**
- User completed ₹10,000 transaction at Amazon (should be Shopping category, preferred merchant)
- Transaction incorrectly tagged as "Other" category by merchant metadata
- System applied 1% rate (₹100 cashback) instead of 5% rate (₹500 cashback)
- User contacts support claiming incorrect cashback amount
- User has ₹200/₹500 earned in Shopping category this month

**User Story:** As a customer support agent, I want to see the merchant category assignment and cashback calculation logic for disputed transactions, so that I can quickly identify misclassifications and initiate corrections without manual calculation.

**Steps:**
1. User contacts support via in-app chat claiming "I should have received ₹500 cashback on my Amazon purchase but only got ₹100"
2. Support agent opens user's account in Support Center
3. Agent navigates to disputed transaction and clicks "View Cashback Calculation Details"
4. Support Center displays: Merchant Name: Amazon, Assigned Category: Other, Preferred Merchant: Yes, Rate Applied: 1%, Amount: ₹100
5. Agent identifies misclassification (should be Shopping category)
6. Agent clicks "Raise Category Correction Request" button
7. System generates ticket with transaction ID, current category, suggested category (Shopping), and cashback difference (₹400)
8. Backend ops team reviews and approves correction within 24 hours
9. System recalculates cashback: ₹10,000 × 5% = ₹500, credits ₹400 difference to user account
10. User receives notification: "Cashback correction processed. ₹400 added to your account for Amazon transaction"

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given transaction category is "Other" but merchant is in preferred merchant list, when support agent views transaction in Support Center, then system displays amber warning flag: "Category mismatch detected - preferred merchant tagged as Other"
- Given agent raises category correction request, when ticket is created, then system automatically calculates cashback difference based on correct category rate and current category cap status, and includes this in ticket metadata
- Given correction approved and processed, when user views transaction details, then updated cashback amount displays with blue info icon and tooltip: "Cashback corrected on [date]. Original: ₹100, Corrected: ₹500"
- Given correction increases category cap usage, when recalculation runs, then system updates Shopping category progress to ₹600/₹500 (cap exhausted) and adjusts subsequent transactions in same month to 1% rate if applicable

**Failure State AC:**
- Given category correction would exceed overall monthly cap of ₹2000, when ops team approves correction, then system credits only the amount up to ₹2000 cap and displays message in Support Center: "Partial correction applied. User at monthly cap limit. Credited ₹[amount] of ₹[requested] difference"
- Given user account is closed or blocked, when correction processing attempts, then system fails gracefully with error logged to ops dashboard: "Cannot process cashback correction - account status: [CLOSED/BLOCKED]" and ticket remains in pending state for manual review

**Priority:** P1

## NON-FUNCTIONAL USE CASES

### Performance Requirements:

- **Transaction Detail Load Time:** Cashback calculation section must render within 800ms of transaction detail screen load on 4G network (p95 latency)
  - **Acceptance:** Measure via APM tools; 95% of requests complete within 800ms; cashback section uses skeleton loader if data not available within 500ms

- **Cashback Calculation Processing:** Real-time cashback amount must be calculated and stored within 5 seconds of transaction settlement posting
  - **Acceptance:** Monitor settlement-to-calculation lag via backend metrics; 99% of transactions processed within 5 seconds; failed calculations retry with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts)

- **Monthly Cap Aggregation Query:** Category-wise and overall cap queries must execute within 200ms to support transaction detail page load
  - **Acceptance:** Database query performance monitoring shows p95 latency <200ms; implement Redis cache for current month cap data with 5-minute TTL

### Security Requirements:

- **Cashback Data Access Control:** Cashback calculation details in Support Center restricted to L2+ support agents with audit logging
  - **Acceptance:** Role-based access control enforced; unauthorized access attempts logged and blocked; audit trail captures agent ID, timestamp, transaction ID, and action taken

- **PII Protection in Cashback Display:** Transaction-level cashback display must not expose full card number or sensitive merchant details beyond masked format
  - **Acceptance:** Card number displayed as "XXXX 1234"; merchant name shown without full address or terminal ID; compliance review confirms no PII leakage

### Accessibility Requirements:

- **Screen Reader Compatibility:** Cashback earned section and category progress bars must be fully navigable and readable via screen readers (WCAG 2.1 AA)
  - **Acceptance:** VoiceOver (iOS) and TalkBack (Android) testing confirms all cashback elements have proper labels; progress bars announce percentage values; color is not sole indicator of cap status

### Reliability Requirements:

- **Graceful Degradation:** If cashback calculation service is unavailable, transaction details must still load with placeholder message and retry mechanism
  - **Acceptance:** Circuit breaker pattern implemented; after 3 failed attempts, display "Cashback details temporarily unavailable" with manual refresh option; transaction core details remain accessible

- **Data Consistency:** Cashback amounts displayed in transaction details must match amounts in monthly statements and rewards ledger within 1-hour reconciliation window
  - **Acceptance:** Automated reconciliation job runs hourly; discrepancies >₹1 trigger alerts to ops team; 99.9% of transactions reconcile without manual intervention
